statement.p: Find the critical point of the function f(x,y)=-\left(25x+5y^{2}+\ln\mathopen{}\left(\left|x+y\right|\right)\right).

Use the Second Derivative Test to determine whether it is
a saddle point
test fails
a local minimum
a local maximum

static.solution:
f(x,y)=-\left(25x+5y^{2}+\ln\mathopen{}\left(\left|x+y\right|\right)\right) equal to zero and solve f_x(x,y)=-\left(25+\frac{1}{x+y}\right)=0 f_y(x,y)=-\left(10y+\frac{1}{x+y}\right)=0 The first equation implies that \frac{1}{x+y}=-25. Substituting into the second equation gives 25-10y=0 \quad \Rightarrow \quad y=2.5 We substitute y=2.5 in the first equation and solve for x: -25-\frac{1}{x+2.5}=0 \quad \Rightarrow \quad x+2.5=\frac{1}{-25} \quad \Rightarrow \quad x=\frac{-2.5 \cdot -25 + 1}{-25}=\frac{63.5}{-25} We obtain critical point \left(\frac{63.5}{-25}, 2.5\right).
Notice, that although f_x and f_y do not exist where x+y=0, these are not critical points, since f is not defined at these points.
Now we compute the Discriminant. We find the second-order partials: f_{xx}(x,y)=\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(-\left(25+\frac{1}{x+y}\right)\right)=\frac{1}{\left(x+y\right)^{2}} f_{yy}(x,y)=\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(-\left(10y+\frac{1}{x+y}\right)\right)=\frac{1}{\left(x+y\right)^{2}}-10 f_{xy}(x,y)=\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(-\left(25+\frac{1}{x+y}\right)\right)=\frac{1}{\left(x+y\right)^{2}} The discriminant is thus D(x,y)=f_{xx}f_{yy}-f_{xy}^2=\frac{1}{\left(x+y\right)^{2}} \cdot \left(\frac{1}{\left(x+y\right)^{2}}-10\right)-\frac{1}{(x+y)^4}=-\frac{10}{\left(x+y\right)^{2}}
Applying the Second Derivative Test we have D\left(\frac{63.5}{-25},2.5\right)=-6250\lt 0 We conclude that f\left(\frac{63.5}{-25},2.5\right) is a saddle point.
